summary: Checked before any route, on every request whatever its method and path - the page at / and a path no route has included - in this order, the first that refuses answering. THE NAME IT WAS SENT TO (its Host): a request whose Host is not one of the server's own names - 127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], the address it listens on (--host), and the host of each page it was started to allow - is refused 403 host_not_allowed. A website whose name is made to point at this machine (DNS rebinding) sends that name as its Host and as its Origin, and would otherwise pass for the server's own page: it is refused whatever it asks, and so is a request with no Origin that names a host the server does not have - a server on this machine has no business answering a name it does not have. A name is compared in lower case and without its port; a Host that is not a name and a port is refused. A request that names no Host at all is answered as before: every browser names one. THE PAGE THAT SENT IT (its Origin): a request that carries an Origin header is refused 403 origin_not_allowed unless its Origin is the server's own - the address the request was sent to: http:// and its Host - or a page's address the server was started to allow (--allow-origin, written as a browser writes a page's address: scheme, host and port). So a web page from anywhere else can never act on the server, not even with a request a browser sends without asking first (a form's POST, or a text body). ITS BODY, whatever the method: a request that names a Transfer-Encoding - a body sent in chunks, its length never said - is refused 411 length_required, whether or not it names a Content-Length too: the server reads a body by its Content-Length alone, and would otherwise read the chunks as a request of their own; a request whose Content-Length is more than the server reads (--max-body, 16 MiB by default) is refused 413 too_large before a byte of its body is read; a Content-Length that is not a whole number of bytes reads as no body. A body within the cap that no route reads - a refused request's, a GET's - is read and set aside, so a connection the browser keeps open stays in step; a body the server does not read - in chunks, or over the cap - is never read at all: its answer says Connection: close, and the connection is closed a moment after the answer is out - so an asker still sending hears the answer, not a reset, and nothing it sent is ever read as a request. ITS TIME: a request must arrive whole - its first line, its headers and its body - within --read-timeout seconds (10 by default) of the server starting to wait for it: of its connection being made, or of the answer before it on a connection kept open. One that has not is never answered: its connection is closed, and a request cut off part way is said in the server's log. Only a page the server was started to allow is ever told it may read an answer: Access-Control-Allow-Origin naming it, and Vary: Origin, on every answer it is given - a refusal before any route included. A refusal for any other page carries no Access-Control header: the browser shows the page nothing. A request with no Origin, sent to one of the server's own names, and one from the server's own page, are answered exactly as if there were no check. An allowed page's preflight - OPTIONS, from that page - is answered 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type. A method no route takes - HEAD, PUT, DELETE, any other - is checked the same way, and then answered 501, as http.server answers a method it does not take; so is OPTIONS with no Origin, or from the server's own page.
